title: Pfalz
description: Germany's sunniest wine region: rich, dry Riesling and rising Pinot Noir in the shelter of the Haardt.
L: The Pfalz, the Palatinate, lies in south-west Germany, a strip about 85 km long between the Haardt mountains, a continuation of France's Vosges, and the Rhine plain. It borders Alsace to the south. With about 23,700 hectares, it's Germany's second largest wine region. The German Wine Route, Deutsche Weinstrasse, runs through it.

The Haardt shelters the Pfalz from westerly rain, as the Vosges do for Alsace. It's one of Germany's sunniest and driest regions, with almonds, figs and even lemons growing. That warmth gives riper grapes and fuller wines than further north. Soils vary: sandstone, limestone, loess, basalt and clay.
What shelters the Pfalz from rain?
The Haardt, a continuation of the Vosges.

The Pfalz has two areas. The Mittelhaardt, in the north, has the most famous villages: Forst, Deidesheim, Wachenheim and Bad Dürkheim, home of historic estates like Bürklin-Wolf, von Buhl and Bassermann-Jordan. The Südliche Weinstrasse, in the south, near Alsace, is a source of exciting Pinot Noir and whites.
The Pfalz is one of Germany's sunniest regions.
Yes. Figs and almonds grow there.
The Pfalz runs along the Haardt, bordering Alsace
Its rain shadow makes it sunny and dry
The Mittelhaardt and the south each have their stars

Riesling is the most planted grape, about 25% of the Pfalz, one of the world's largest Riesling areas. The warm climate gives ripe peach, apricot and citrus, with fuller body and good acidity. Most is dry. The Mittelhaardt villages make some of Germany's greatest Rieslings.

Spätburgunder, Pinot Noir, has grown fast in the south, alongside Weissburgunder, Pinot Blanc, and Grauburgunder, Pinot Gris. Dornfelder, a dark red cross, is popular for everyday wine. Müller-Thurgau, Silvaner, Scheurebe and Gewürztraminer also grow here. The Pfalz is Germany's most diverse region.
Match each German name to its grape.
The Pfalz grows a wide range of grapes.
The Südpfalz, near Alsace, is a source of excellent Spätburgunder. Producers like Friedrich Becker grow vines right on the French border.
Which is the Pfalz's most planted grape?
Riesling, about a quarter of vineyards.
Riesling leads, ripe and mostly dry
The Pinot family is rising, especially in the south

For much of the 20th century, German Riesling abroad meant sweet. From the 1980s, Pfalz producers led a return to dry, trocken, Riesling, which had been traditional before. Today over two-thirds of German wine is dry or off-dry, and the Pfalz's warm climate makes balanced dry wines easier.

Dry Pfalz Riesling is fuller and riper than Mosel or Rheingau Riesling, often 12.5 to 13.5% alcohol, with stone fruit, citrus, spice and minerality from sandstone, limestone or basalt. GG wines from top sites, like Forster Kirchenstück, Forster Jesuitengarten and Deidesheimer Hohenmorgen, can age 10 to 20 years.
How does dry Pfalz Riesling typically compare with Mosel Riesling?
A warmer climate gives more body and ripeness.

Forst's top vineyards have basalt, volcanic rock, which absorbs heat and gives intense, spicy, mineral wines. Kirchenstück, a small walled site in Forst, is often considered one of Germany's finest dry Riesling vineyards. Labels name village and vineyard, like Forster Pechstein.
Wehlener Sonnenuhr is in the Mosel.

Reading the Pfalz and eating with it

Labels show producer, village plus vineyard, like Forster Pechstein, the grape, and trocken or GG for dry wines. VDP estates use Gutswein, Ortswein, Erste Lage and Grosse Lage. Some producers use Prädikat terms only for sweet wines. The Pfalz also makes Sekt, sparkling wine.

The Pfalz's food is hearty: Saumagen, stuffed pig's stomach, a regional speciality; Flammkuchen, a thin bacon and onion tart; sausages and sauerkraut; and chestnuts. Dry Riesling suits pork, sausages and Flammkuchen; Spätburgunder suits game and duck; Scheurebe suits spicy food. Serve Riesling at 8 to 11 degrees.
Which regional Pfalz dish is a classic with dry Riesling?
Stuffed pig's stomach is a Pfalz speciality.
In the Pfalz, wine is often served in a Dubbeglas, a dimpled half-litre glass, at village wine festivals like the Dürkheimer Wurstmarkt.
The Pfalz makes mostly sweet Riesling.
Not true. Most Pfalz Riesling is dry.
